chapter: Own sound and the film Bird
title: Parker's influence and how individual style gets recognized
summary: Alto players get compared to Parker because of the instrument; a style must be heard widely before differences are recognized.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah. Well Louis Armstrong seemed to have the same — up until Parker he was kind of I guess the man who set the standard and most people were compared to him, especially the trumpet players, would be compared with him.

Yeah, right. And you know the differences that manifest itself in a particular person, has to be heard in the public consciousness long enough for the difference to be solidified in other people’s minds. You know what I mean? For them to say oh, this is a different style, this is Roy Eldridge. You know what I mean? Whatever that difference is, it has to be heard often enough by enough people, musicians, whatever, to be able to discern the little bit of difference. Because no two people are exactly alike. And the differences have to be discerned. Once they are discerned by enough people, industry people, other musicians, critics, writers, whomever is visible enough or heard enough for the people to know the difference between this and say Charlie Parker or Louis Armstrong, then that difference is no longer like this anymore, it’s like this, because it’s known. You see what I mean? And that’s what happened to some people. You know if a martian came down to earth and listened to say Dizzy Gillespie, and say listened to Pete Candoli, to him it would sound the same. You know what I’m saying? But not to us, because if you know Pete and you know his style kind of sounds sort of like that, and Dizzy is this and that. But to a martian well it’s like well it’s the same one. What’s the difference? And these little bit of difference only becomes bigger when you have isolated that difference.
